title: GMOCAT: A Graph-Enhanced Multi-Objective Method for Computerized Adaptive Testing

problem.claim: CAT must select questions for students while balancing accurate ability prediction, concept diversity, and question exposure control.

gap.claim: Most existing methods focus on ability prediction and ignore concept diversity, question exposure control, and relational information between questions and knowledge concepts.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes GMOCAT, a graph-enhanced multi-objective method for computerized adaptive testing.
GMOCAT introduces quality, diversity, and novelty objectives into scalarized multi-objective reinforcement learning and uses an Actor-Critic Recommender to optimize them simultaneously.
GMOCAT uses a graph neural network to learn relation-aware embeddings of questions and concepts by aggregating neighborhood information from relation graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on three real-world educational datasets.
The authors report that GMOCAT outperforms state-of-the-art methods on ability prediction and performs better on concept diversity and question exposure.

narrative_sequence.summary: CAT adaptively selects questions using students' historical response records.
Data-driven CAT methods improve performance over heuristic methods, but existing approaches commonly prioritize ability prediction alone.
Existing methods neglect diversity, exposure control, and relational information between questions and concepts.
GMOCAT combines multi-objective reinforcement learning, an Actor-Critic Recommender, and graph neural network embeddings.
Experiments on three real-world educational datasets are reported to show improvements across ability prediction, concept diversity, and question exposure.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly optimizes prediction quality, concept diversity, and question exposure through scalarized multi-objective reinforcement learning.

interpretation.claim: When a sequential recommendation problem has competing quality and coverage objectives, explicitly modeling them together may address limitations of single-objective optimization.

application.claim: Apply multi-objective optimization when adaptive question selection must balance predictive accuracy with diversity and exposure control.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the objectives, scalarization weights, or trade-offs generalize beyond the reported educational datasets.

source_observation.claim: The method learns relation-aware question and concept embeddings from relational graphs.

interpretation.claim: Relational structure in response data may provide useful signals for adaptive selection that are unavailable from isolated question features.

application.claim: Use graph-based representations when items and concepts are connected through meaningful educational or behavioral relations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the graph construction, the quality of the relational data, or whether the approach remains effective when such relations are sparse or noisy.

unknowns: Dataset names, sizes, and splits are not provided.
Evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and quantitative effect sizes are not provided.
Scalarization weights, training details, ablations, and implementation details are not provided.
